text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand this infant has recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing; to begin our assessment, how old is the patient and what specific activities seem to trigger these breathing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The clinical presentation of stridor and wheezing exacerbated by crying, feeding, and neck flexion, accompanied by post-feeding vomiting, is classic for this condition. No further tests are required to confirm this diagnosis.
